1	# Styles
2	
3	This file is the visual vocabulary: **what it looks like**. [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)
4	is the technique arsenal: **how you render it**. They are separate on purpose, and
5	collapsing them is how runs end up templated.
6	
7	The distinction is sharp because techniques carry no opinion. `backdrop-filter`
8	builds the layered translucency of liquid glass, and it also builds the flat frosted
9	panels of a Swiss layout where the blur is the only softness on the page. A noise
10	shader is film grain in a cinematic grade and paper tooth in a risograph print. A
11	spring is playful in a claymorphic world and clinical in a blueprint. The style is
12	the opinion; the technique is a means of getting there.
13	
14	The order is fixed. **Style is chosen at Gate B1 with the concept**, from the brief,
15	the archetype, and the vision. **Techniques are assigned in Loop 2b to serve the
16	style already chosen.** Reaching for a style because you want to use a shader is the
17	tail wagging the dog, and it shows in the output. Everything below is a starting
18	position under `§3`. Read [the guardrails](#the-guardrails) before you pick.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Surface and material
23	
24	**Glassmorphism.** Translucent panels over a substrate worth seeing through to,
25	legible from the blur behind them, never from a fill. Depth reads as blur radius,
26	nearest layer blurring hardest, each panel edged with a 1px light-catching border.
27	**Implies** `backdrop-filter`, z-layering, `color-mix()` borders. **Fails** as gray
28	rectangles on a flat background, and breaks `§12` under body copy. **Right when** the
29	background is itself content.
30	
31	**Liquid glass.** Apple's 2025 material language, where the panel refracts rather
32	than merely blurs: content bends passing under the edge, specular highlights track
33	the light, the shape lenses on scroll. Real implementation is an SDF and shader job;
34	`backdrop-filter` alone gets glassmorphism with a borrowed name. **Implies** WebGL,
35	an SDF panel, scroll-linked light, a hard `§13` budget. **Fails** as chrome that
36	buries the work (`§7`). **Right when** the work is material or hardware.
37	
38	**Neumorphism / soft UI.** Every element extruded from one background hue by a
39	matched shadow pair, dark and light, cast from a single committed angle. No borders
40	and almost no color: form is entirely shadow, in one narrow tonal band. It fails
41	contrast by default and ships only with the fix in
42	[Style and accessibility](#style-and-accessibility). **Implies** dual `box-shadow`,
43	one hue. **Fails** as putty with invisible affordances. **Right when** exactly one
44	object is extruded and the rest is flat.
45	
46	**Claymorphism.** Inflated rounded volumes with large radii, soft occlusion at the
47	base, a bright saturated palette, and heavy rounded type. Objects read as pressable
48	toys with thickness, lifted by a diffuse colored shadow. **Implies** big
49	`border-radius`, layered colored shadows, spring press. **Fails** as childish, which
50	sinks a senior portfolio faster than anything here. **Right when** the work is
51	consumer and the copy stays serious.
52	
53	**Skeuomorphic revival.** Real material simulation, never nostalgic gloss: paper
54	with visible fiber, ink bleeding into it, embossed metal with a directional brush,
55	edges worn where a thumb rests. One material, simulated honestly. **Implies**
56	generated textures per `§10`, displacement maps, per-material lighting. **Fails** as
57	2010 iOS pastiche the moment two materials share a surface. **Right when** the work
58	has a physical antecedent.
59	
60	**Aerogel / frosted depth.** Milky diffuse layers with no light source, where depth
61	reads as accumulated haze and nothing has a hard edge. Separation comes from density,
62	the palette stays desaturated, light bleeds between planes. **Implies** stacked
63	low-opacity fills, large soft blurs, a fog gradient. **Fails** as washed-out mush
64	when every layer sits at one density. **Right when** hierarchy rides on type alone.
65	
66	## Structural
67	
68	**Swiss / International.** A visible modular grid, one family at a strict scale,
69	flush-left ragged-right setting, objective photography on grid intersections.
70	Whitespace is structural, color appears once, every alignment is provable against the
71	column. **Implies** CSS Grid with named lines, a mathematical scale, one `§8` accent.
72	**Fails** as an agency template, the most-copied system in design. **Right when**
73	dense work needs an authoritative frame, with a collision applied.
74	
75	**Brutalism.** Raw HTML honesty: system fonts, default link blue, visible borders,
76	unstyled form controls, layout that reveals the DOM instead of disguising it.
77	**Implies** near-zero CSS, system font stacks, native controls, no motion.
78	**Fails** as an excuse for laziness, indistinguishable from an unfinished build.
79	**Right when** credibility comes from substance and refusing to decorate is the
80	position.
81	
82	**Neo-brutalism.** Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, saturated
83	flat blocks, heavy grotesque type at aggressive sizes. Elements rotate slightly and
84	overlap without softening; interaction moves the shadow, never fades anything.
85	**Implies** solid `box-shadow` offsets, 2-4px borders, transform on hover.
86	**Fails** as Gumroad cosplay, the most saturated style on the web right now.
87	**Right when** the collision partner supplies the restraint.
88	
89	**Bento.** A dense grid of unequal self-contained cards sized by importance rather
90	than content length, uniform radii, consistent gaps, reading as one object at a
91	glance. **Implies** CSS Grid with spanning areas, container queries, per-card art
92	direction. **Fails** as a dashboard with nothing to show, and hides narrative because
93	every card is equal in reading order. **Right when** many small things matter at once.
94	
95	**Editorial / print.** Magazine mechanics carried honestly onto screen: measured
96	columns, real hyphenation, drop caps on the baseline grid, pull quotes breaking the
97	measure, marginalia, running heads and folios. Type does the work; images are plates.
98	**Implies** `hyphens`, `text-wrap: pretty`, `initial-letter`, a serif with optical
99	sizes, self-hosted per `§9`. **Fails** past a 75-character measure, or when columns
100	force scroll-up reading on mobile. **Right when** the case studies are long.
101	
102	**Swiss-punk / Ray Gun.** The Swiss grid built, then deliberately violated: type
103	overlapping, rotated, set in conflicting families, letters cropped by the viewport.
104	Type becomes image and legibility becomes a variable the designer controls.
105	**Implies** absolute positioning over a grid, `mix-blend-mode`, variable-font
106	extremes. **Fails** as noise when the grid was never built, since the violation only
107	reads against visible order. **Right when** the audience reads sophistication.
108	
109	## Atmospheric
110	
111	**Cinematic dark.** A single key light with real falloff, deep vignette, grain sized
112	to the viewport, blacks lifted and tinted. Content sits in pools of light and the
113	space between them is genuinely dark. **Implies** radial key, grain shader or SVG
114	turbulence, LUT via `feColorMatrix`, controlled bloom. **Fails** when the grade
115	crushes body copy below 4.5:1 and grain eats small type. **Right when** the work
116	benefits from being lit.
117	
118	**Aurora / mesh gradient.** Large soft color fields drifting across each other with
119	no visible edges and no repeat. OKLCH interpolation keeps midpoints saturated instead
120	of gray, and motion is slow enough to be felt without being watched. **Implies**
121	OKLCH gradients, canvas or WebGL mesh, grain against banding. **Fails** as the
122	default AI landing page, the most generated look of the last three years.
123	**Right when** it is a substrate for another style.
124	
125	**Glow / neon.** A dark substrate with emissive accents that actually bloom, light
126	spilling past its source and tinting what it lands on. Edges glow from the inside,
127	shadows take the accent hue, two emissive colors at most. **Implies** layered
128	`box-shadow` bloom or a real bloom pass, dark tokens, hue-matched shadows.
129	**Fails** as halation that makes every string of text fringe. **Right when** the
130	emission points at the work.
131	
132	**Vaporwave / Y2K.** Chromed type with environment reflection, cyan and magenta
133	gradient meshes, CRT scanlines and phosphor bleed, grids receding to a horizon,
134	deliberate JPEG and VHS artifacts. The nostalgia is specific to 1995-2003 hardware
135	and reads as costume unless committed to fully. **Implies** SVG chrome gradients, a
136	CRT shader, chromatic aberration, dithering. **Fails** as kitsch that dates the
137	subject. **Right when** the audience shares the reference.
138	
139	**Solarpunk.** Organic growth forms and botanical geometry under warm optimistic
140	light: curves derived from phyllotaxis, never arbitrary blobs, terracotta and sage
141	and brass, layouts that branch instead of stacking. **Implies** generative SVG
142	growth, warm gradients, curved layout paths, organic easing. **Fails** as generic
143	eco-branding with a leaf icon and a green button. **Right when** the work is climate,
144	agriculture, health, or civic.
145	
146	## Motion-native
147	
148	In these four the behavior **is** the aesthetic. A still screenshot cannot represent
149	them, which makes the `§12` reduced-motion design a first-class deliverable.
150	
151	**Kinetic.** Nothing is at rest: type in perpetual motion, marquees running at
152	different rates by depth, letters responding to pointer velocity, composition
153	recomposing continuously. Stillness is used once, as punctuation. **Implies**
154	scroll-velocity input, variable-font axis animation, transform-only compositing.
155	**Fails** as exhausting, and unreadable when the thing in motion is the thing being
156	read. **Right when** the work is performance or sound.
157	
158	**Physics-world.** Spring, inertia, mass, and collision are the interaction model.
159	Elements have weight, throwing them works, they settle rather than snap, and they
160	occupy space other elements respect. Nothing uses a duration; everything uses a
161	stiffness. **Implies** a physics loop, spring tokens instead of easing curves, a
162	valid resting layout. **Fails** as a toy when the physics never resolves into
163	something readable. **Right when** the play makes a point.
164	
165	**Scroll-cinema.** The page is a film reel scrubbed by the scrollbar: scroll position
166	maps to a timeline, sections pin while their contents advance, and the sequence has
167	shots, cuts, and cadence. **Implies** pinned containers, scrubbed timelines,
168	`will-change` discipline, a real `§13` budget. **Fails** as hijacked scroll that
169	fights the user and strands anyone landing mid-page. **Right when** the work has
170	narrative order and one story to tell.
171	
172	**Spatial / 3D-world.** The site is a navigable space with camera, depth, and
173	position. Sections are places, navigation is movement, and the sense of where you are
174	does the work a menu usually does. **Implies** WebGL or CSS 3D, a camera rig,
175	level-of-detail, a no-WebGL fallback per `§12`. **Fails** as a maze where nobody
176	finds the case study, which is `§7` violated structurally. **Right when** a flat page
177	would misrepresent the work.
178	
179	## Technical and data
180	
181	**Terminal.** Monospace throughout on a real fixed cell grid, blinking block cursor,
182	phosphor color on near-black, scanlines and slight CRT curvature at the edges, output
183	persisting in scrollback. **Implies** `ch` units, a monospace with box-drawing
184	coverage, a CRT shader, typed-output timing. **Fails** as a gimmick with a fake
185	prompt that takes three commands and breaks on the fourth. **Right when** the
186	terminal is where the subject's work happens.
187	
188	**Blueprint.** Drawing conventions applied literally: dimension lines with arrowheads
189	and measurements, section callouts, leader lines to annotations, hatching, a title
190	block, a consistent line-weight hierarchy. **Implies** SVG line work, precise stroke
191	tokens, annotation positioning, a drafting typeface. **Fails** as decoration when the
192	dimensions are fake and measure nothing. **Right when** the callouts annotate real
193	work.
194	
195	**Data-brutalist.** Dense tables, sparklines, and charts as the aesthetic itself,
196	never as supporting evidence. Rules are hairlines, numbers tabular, alignment
197	decimal, and the interest comes from the density of true information. **Implies**
198	`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, table semantics, inline SVG charts. **Fails**
199	the moment the numbers are decorative, which breaks `§5` outright. **Right when**
200	`EVIDENCE.md` can carry every number on the page.
201	
202	**Wireframe / vector.** Line art only: no fills, hidden-line removal, contours
203	describing volume through stroke alone, weight variation carrying depth. **Implies**
204	SVG or WebGL line rendering, hidden-line computation, stroke-only tokens, draw-on
205	animation. **Fails** as thin and cold at sizes where strokes vanish. **Right when**
206	the work is structural and the outline is the honest view.
207	
208	## Textural
209	
210	**Risograph.** Two or three spot inks printed in separate passes with visible
211	misregistration, halftone dots in the shadows, paper grain showing through, and
212	overprint areas producing a third color neither ink has. **Implies** separated
213	channels, `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, per-channel offset, a halftone shader, paper
214	per `§10`. **Fails** as a filter when the misregistration is uniform, since real
215	registration error drifts. **Right when** the subject prints.
216	
217	**Xerox / degraded.** Photocopy artifacts as the medium: blown highlights, crushed
218	blacks, toner scatter at the edges, a slight skew, and generational loss where a copy
219	of a copy has lost its midtones. **Implies** threshold and dither passes, noise
220	displacement, per-element skew, a high-contrast duotone. **Fails** as illegible on
221	body copy instead of on images and headers. **Right when** the work is zine or
222	archival.
223	
224	**Collage.** Layered scraps at mixed scale with torn edges, tape and staples, cast
225	shadows from real height differences, elements rotated off axis. The composition is
226	assembled, never laid out. **Implies** irregular SVG masks, per-element shadow
227	and rotation, generated paper and tape, deliberate z-order. **Fails** as chaos with
228	no reading order, losing `§6` immediately. **Right when** the practice is genuinely
229	multidisciplinary.
230	
231	**Ink / sumi.** Brush dynamics as the whole language: strokes with real pressure
232	variation, wet bleed into fiber, dry-brush breakup at speed, negative space treated
233	as the subject. One color, one gesture per composition. **Implies** SVG
234	variable-width paths, bleed via displacement, generated fiber, stroke-order
235	animation. **Fails** as a stock brush texture, which reads as clip art instantly.
236	**Right when** restraint is the position.
237	
238	## Reductive
239	
240	**Radical minimalism.** Type and space, nothing else: no borders, no cards, no
241	shadows, no illustration. Hierarchy comes only from size, weight, and distance, and
242	the whitespace is measured, never left over. **Implies** one family with real
243	weights, a precise spatial scale, optical alignment, single-property motion.
244	**Fails** as unmemorable when the copy is weak, since there is nothing else to look
245	at. **Right when** the writing is strong.
246	
247	**Monochrome plus one accent.** A single hue's full tonal range carries structure,
248	and exactly one accent sampled from reality per `§8` appears only where attention
249	must go. The accent never decorates. **Implies** an OKLCH lightness ramp, one accent
250	token, usage rules stated in `DIRECTION.md`. **Fails** as forgettable, the most
251	common way a run looks competent and generic at once. **Right when** it is the
252	discipline layer under a louder partner.
253	
254	**ASCII / text-only.** The page is characters: art drawn in a fixed cell grid, layout
255	built from box-drawing glyphs, images dithered into character density. Nothing is
256	rendered that could not be pasted into a text file. **Implies** monospace with full
257	box-drawing coverage, `ch` and `lh` units, semantic HTML underneath per `§12`.
258	**Fails** as unreadable to screen readers and unusable below 400px. **Right when**
259	the constraint is the point.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Collision
264	
265	This is the most important section in the file. A single named style is one search
266	away from being everyone else's site. The un-templated work lives where two styles
267	are held in tension, because the constraints of one force the other to behave in ways
268	its own tradition never asks of it.
269	
270	| Collision | What it produces that neither parent has |
271	|---|---|
272	| **Liquid glass over a blueprint substrate** | A technical drawing is flat and authoritative by convention. Put a refractive lens over it and the dimension lines bend as you scroll, so precision becomes something you look *through*. The drawing gains depth without losing its claim to accuracy. |
273	| **Risograph texture on a Swiss grid** | The grid asserts machine order; the misregistration asserts a hand and a press. Together they read as a printed object instead of a rendered page, and the grid stops looking like every other agency site because it is visibly ink. |
274	| **Terminal chrome around a physics world** | The monospace frame promises determinism and fixed cells. The contents obey springs and collide. A frame that cannot bend around contents that will not sit still is the whole idea, and neither style contains it alone. |
275	| **Editorial print with a spatial 3D reveal** | Columns, drop caps, marginalia, then the page turns out to have depth and the columns are planes standing in space. Reading becomes navigation and the reader's position in the document becomes literal. |
276	| **Brutalist structure with a cinematic grade** | Raw exposed structure and system fonts, lit with a single key and a vignette. The honesty stops reading as unfinished and starts reading as staged, a claim neither raw HTML nor a film grade makes on its own. |
277	| **Neumorphism inside radical minimalism** | The style that normally fails by covering a page in soft mush is reduced to one extruded object in an empty field. It becomes sculptural, and the contrast failure disappears because nothing has to be read off it. |
278	| **Ink gesture across data-brutalism** | Dense tabular numbers with one brush stroke laid over them. The gesture asserts that a person read these numbers and had a view, which a table cannot say and a painting cannot evidence. |
279	| **Vaporwave chrome under Swiss typography** | Y2K materials disciplined by an unforgiving grid and one type family. The nostalgia survives, the kitsch collapse does not, because the layout refuses to join in. |
280	
281	**Picking a collision that serves the brief.** One parent comes from the archetype and
282	positioning in `BRAND.md`. The other comes from something materially true about the
283	subject: their medium, their tools, the physical object their work becomes, the room
284	they work in. Both must be defensible in one sentence each against `BRIEF.md`. If
285	only one is defensible, you have a style plus a decoration, and the decoration reads
286	as arbitrary to everyone who sees it.
287	
288	**The load-bearing rule:** one parent carries structure, the other carries surface.
289	Two structural parents fight over the grid and produce mush. Two surface parents
290	produce noise with no bones. Name which parent is which in `DIRECTION.md` before you
291	build anything.
292	
293	## Subversion
294	
295	The second route out of template. Take one style and break exactly one of its own
296	rules, and the rule you break has to be the one the style is most identified by.
297	Break two and you have a different style executed badly.
298	
299	- **Swiss where one element never obeys the grid.** A single photographic plate hangs
300	  past the margin in every section, at the same overhang each time. The grid is
301	  provable everywhere else, which is what makes the overhang read as a decision.
302	- **Brutalism with immaculate type.** Everything raw, default, unstyled, except the
303	  typography, which gets real optical sizing, hyphenation, and hung punctuation. The
304	  refusal to decorate becomes selective and therefore intentional.
305	- **Cinematic dark that turns the lights on once.** One section drops the grade
306	  entirely and goes flat daylight white. The return to darkness afterwards hits
307	  harder than the darkness ever did alone.
308	- **Glassmorphism with no blur.** The panels refract and catch light at their edges
309	  and nothing behind them softens. Legibility improves, `§12` gets easier, and the
310	  material reads as harder and more precise than glass usually does.
311	- **Editorial print where the margin is the main column.** Marginalia carries the
312	  primary narrative and the body text becomes the aside. The reader learns a new
313	  hierarchy in about four seconds and remembers it.
314	- **Terminal with one full-color photograph.** Everything is phosphor and monospace
315	  except a single image at full fidelity. It becomes the most important object on the
316	  site with no layout emphasis at all.
317	
318	State the broken rule explicitly in `DIRECTION.md`. A subversion nobody can name is
319	indistinguishable from an inconsistency.
320	
321	## The guardrails
322	
323	This section is `§3` enforced.
324	
325	- **The vocabulary names a starting position, never a destination.** Ship a named
326	  style unmodified and the run failed. No entry above is a finished answer.
327	- **Every run states in `DIRECTION.md` what it did to the style that nobody else
328	  does** — the collision, subversion, or invention applied, in one sentence a
329	  stranger could check the site against.
330	- **The vision beats the style.** If the vision or `BRIEF.md` says "quiet, like a
331	  printed book," liquid glass is off the table regardless of how good the prototype
332	  looks. A prototype is not an argument against the intake from `§0`.
333	- **The archetype from `BRAND.md` pulls a shortlist, never a single answer.** It
334	  narrows the field to three or four candidates. Treating it as a lookup table is how
335	  every Sage becomes Swiss and every Creator becomes neo-brutalist.
336	- **Anti-positioning from `BRAND.md` bans styles outright.** If the strategy says
337	  "never look like a crypto site," glow-neon and chrome are gone. Honor it as
338	  absolutely as the `§0` do-nots.
339	- **The list is open.** Invent one, name it, describe it in the format above, and add
340	  it to the run. An invented style with a real name and stated mechanics beats the
341	  best-executed entry on this page, because nobody can pattern-match it.
342	
343	## Style and accessibility
344	
345	`§12` is **[HARD]**. These styles fight it hardest, and each ships with its fix or
346	does not ship.
347	
348	| Style | What it fights | The fix that ships |
349	|---|---|---|
350	| **Neumorphism** | Form is shadow on one hue, so nothing has a contrast ratio | Extrusion is for containers only. Every label, value, and control state gets a real foreground token at ≥4.5:1. Focus is a hard visible ring, never a deeper shadow. |
351	| **Glassmorphism / liquid glass** | Text contrast changes with whatever scrolls behind it | An opaque or near-opaque scrim behind every text run, measured against the *worst* frame of the moving substrate, never a screenshot. |
352	| **Cinematic dark** | Vignette, grade, and grain push small type below threshold | Measure contrast on the rendered pixels after grade and grain, not on the tokens. Body copy stays out of the vignette falloff. Grain opacity drops on text layers. |
353	| **Kinetic / physics / scroll-cinema** | Motion is the design, so removing motion removes the site | An art-directed still per `§12`: a composed frame with type at rest that someone designed. Scroll-cinema degrades to a paginated document, same content, same order. |
354	| **Spatial / 3D-world** | Navigation depends on a camera and a GPU | Keyboard traversal between named places, a text route to every section, and a no-WebGL fallback that is a real page, never an apology. |
355	| **Terminal** | Scanlines and CRT curvature reduce legibility and can trigger | Curvature and scanline opacity behind `prefers-reduced-motion` plus a visible toggle. Body text renders on the flat layer above the effect. |
356	| **ASCII / text-only** | Screen readers read the art as character soup | `aria-hidden` on the art, `role="img"` with a written alt on the block, and real semantic HTML carrying the content underneath. |
357	| **Glow-neon / vaporwave** | Saturated emission on dark causes halation and fringing | Glow applies to non-text elements only. Text uses a desaturated stop of the same hue at full contrast. Chromatic aberration never touches a glyph. |
358	| **Data-brutalist** | Density defeats zoom and reflow | Real table semantics with scoped headers, horizontal scroll containers that are keyboard reachable, and a stated minimum readable width. |
359	
360	## Light and dark as two designs
361	
362	Per [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)'s art-directed modes, a style often needs a genuinely
363	different treatment in each mode. Never `filter: invert()`. Choose per-mode ink,
364	substrate, shadow direction, and accent chroma deliberately. These break under naive
365	inversion:
366	
367	- **Neumorphism.** Inverting the shadow pair puts the light source underneath, which
368	  no physical object does. Keep the light direction identical in both modes and
369	  change only the surface hue and the shadow spread.
370	- **Glassmorphism.** Blur reads as depth on dark and as haze on light. Light mode
371	  needs more opacity, a heavier border, and less blur to say the same thing.
372	- **Cinematic dark.** There is no light version of a lit set. Light mode is a second
373	  art direction: a printed still with the grade baked in as a duotone, no vignette,
374	  no bloom.
375	- **Glow / neon.** Emission requires darkness. In light mode the glow becomes ink
376	  saturation and weight, and the accent moves from emissive to dense.
377	- **Risograph.** Paper is the substrate. Dark mode is a black-paper print run with
378	  inks chosen for it, and the halftone dot inverts to open rather than filled.
379	- **Blueprint.** White-on-blue and blue-on-white are both real print conventions.
380	  Switch between them on purpose, with line weights retuned, since hairlines that
381	  read on dark disappear on white.
382	- **Aurora / mesh.** OKLCH stops that stay saturated on dark go chalky on light. Each
383	  mode needs its own stop list, never a lightness shift.
384	
385	Declare in `DIRECTION.md` whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or two
386	art directions. If the chosen style appears above, the answer is two art directions,
387	and both get built and screenshotted under `§14`.

# Styles

This file is the visual vocabulary: **what it looks like**. [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)
is the technique arsenal: **how you render it**. They are separate on purpose, and
collapsing them is how runs end up templated.

The distinction is sharp because techniques carry no opinion. `backdrop-filter`
builds the layered translucency of liquid glass, and it also builds the flat frosted
panels of a Swiss layout where the blur is the only softness on the page. A noise
shader is film grain in a cinematic grade and paper tooth in a risograph print. A
spring is playful in a claymorphic world and clinical in a blueprint. The style is
the opinion; the technique is a means of getting there.

The order is fixed. **Style is chosen at Gate B1 with the concept**, from the brief,
the archetype, and the vision. **Techniques are assigned in Loop 2b to serve the
style already chosen.** Reaching for a style because you want to use a shader is the
tail wagging the dog, and it shows in the output. Everything below is a starting
position under `§3`. Read [the guardrails](#the-guardrails) before you pick.

---

## Surface and material

**Glassmorphism.** Translucent panels over a substrate worth seeing through to,
legible from the blur behind them, never from a fill. Depth reads as blur radius,
nearest layer blurring hardest, each panel edged with a 1px light-catching border.
**Implies** `backdrop-filter`, z-layering, `color-mix()` borders. **Fails** as gray
rectangles on a flat background, and breaks `§12` under body copy. **Right when** the
background is itself content.

**Liquid glass.** Apple's 2025 material language, where the panel refracts rather
than merely blurs: content bends passing under the edge, specular highlights track
the light, the shape lenses on scroll. Real implementation is an SDF and shader job;
`backdrop-filter` alone gets glassmorphism with a borrowed name. **Implies** WebGL,
an SDF panel, scroll-linked light, a hard `§13` budget. **Fails** as chrome that
buries the work (`§7`). **Right when** the work is material or hardware.

**Neumorphism / soft UI.** Every element extruded from one background hue by a
matched shadow pair, dark and light, cast from a single committed angle. No borders
and almost no color: form is entirely shadow, in one narrow tonal band. It fails
contrast by default and ships only with the fix in
[Style and accessibility](#style-and-accessibility). **Implies** dual `box-shadow`,
one hue. **Fails** as putty with invisible affordances. **Right when** exactly one
object is extruded and the rest is flat.

**Claymorphism.** Inflated rounded volumes with large radii, soft occlusion at the
base, a bright saturated palette, and heavy rounded type. Objects read as pressable
toys with thickness, lifted by a diffuse colored shadow. **Implies** big
`border-radius`, layered colored shadows, spring press. **Fails** as childish, which
sinks a senior portfolio faster than anything here. **Right when** the work is
consumer and the copy stays serious.

**Skeuomorphic revival.** Real material simulation, never nostalgic gloss: paper
with visible fiber, ink bleeding into it, embossed metal with a directional brush,
edges worn where a thumb rests. One material, simulated honestly. **Implies**
generated textures per `§10`, displacement maps, per-material lighting. **Fails** as
2010 iOS pastiche the moment two materials share a surface. **Right when** the work
has a physical antecedent.

**Aerogel / frosted depth.** Milky diffuse layers with no light source, where depth
reads as accumulated haze and nothing has a hard edge. Separation comes from density,
the palette stays desaturated, light bleeds between planes. **Implies** stacked
low-opacity fills, large soft blurs, a fog gradient. **Fails** as washed-out mush
when every layer sits at one density. **Right when** hierarchy rides on type alone.

## Structural

**Swiss / International.** A visible modular grid, one family at a strict scale,
flush-left ragged-right setting, objective photography on grid intersections.
Whitespace is structural, color appears once, every alignment is provable against the
column. **Implies** CSS Grid with named lines, a mathematical scale, one `§8` accent.
**Fails** as an agency template, the most-copied system in design. **Right when**
dense work needs an authoritative frame, with a collision applied.

**Brutalism.** Raw HTML honesty: system fonts, default link blue, visible borders,
unstyled form controls, layout that reveals the DOM instead of disguising it.
**Implies** near-zero CSS, system font stacks, native controls, no motion.
**Fails** as an excuse for laziness, indistinguishable from an unfinished build.
**Right when** credibility comes from substance and refusing to decorate is the
position.

**Neo-brutalism.** Thick black borders, hard offset shadows with no blur, saturated
flat blocks, heavy grotesque type at aggressive sizes. Elements rotate slightly and
overlap without softening; interaction moves the shadow, never fades anything.
**Implies** solid `box-shadow` offsets, 2-4px borders, transform on hover.
**Fails** as Gumroad cosplay, the most saturated style on the web right now.
**Right when** the collision partner supplies the restraint.

**Bento.** A dense grid of unequal self-contained cards sized by importance rather
than content length, uniform radii, consistent gaps, reading as one object at a
glance. **Implies** CSS Grid with spanning areas, container queries, per-card art
direction. **Fails** as a dashboard with nothing to show, and hides narrative because
every card is equal in reading order. **Right when** many small things matter at once.

**Editorial / print.** Magazine mechanics carried honestly onto screen: measured
columns, real hyphenation, drop caps on the baseline grid, pull quotes breaking the
measure, marginalia, running heads and folios. Type does the work; images are plates.
**Implies** `hyphens`, `text-wrap: pretty`, `initial-letter`, a serif with optical
sizes, self-hosted per `§9`. **Fails** past a 75-character measure, or when columns
force scroll-up reading on mobile. **Right when** the case studies are long.

**Swiss-punk / Ray Gun.** The Swiss grid built, then deliberately violated: type
overlapping, rotated, set in conflicting families, letters cropped by the viewport.
Type becomes image and legibility becomes a variable the designer controls.
**Implies** absolute positioning over a grid, `mix-blend-mode`, variable-font
extremes. **Fails** as noise when the grid was never built, since the violation only
reads against visible order. **Right when** the audience reads sophistication.

## Atmospheric

**Cinematic dark.** A single key light with real falloff, deep vignette, grain sized
to the viewport, blacks lifted and tinted. Content sits in pools of light and the
space between them is genuinely dark. **Implies** radial key, grain shader or SVG
turbulence, LUT via `feColorMatrix`, controlled bloom. **Fails** when the grade
crushes body copy below 4.5:1 and grain eats small type. **Right when** the work
benefits from being lit.

**Aurora / mesh gradient.** Large soft color fields drifting across each other with
no visible edges and no repeat. OKLCH interpolation keeps midpoints saturated instead
of gray, and motion is slow enough to be felt without being watched. **Implies**
OKLCH gradients, canvas or WebGL mesh, grain against banding. **Fails** as the
default AI landing page, the most generated look of the last three years.
**Right when** it is a substrate for another style.

**Glow / neon.** A dark substrate with emissive accents that actually bloom, light
spilling past its source and tinting what it lands on. Edges glow from the inside,
shadows take the accent hue, two emissive colors at most. **Implies** layered
`box-shadow` bloom or a real bloom pass, dark tokens, hue-matched shadows.
**Fails** as halation that makes every string of text fringe. **Right when** the
emission points at the work.

**Vaporwave / Y2K.** Chromed type with environment reflection, cyan and magenta
gradient meshes, CRT scanlines and phosphor bleed, grids receding to a horizon,
deliberate JPEG and VHS artifacts. The nostalgia is specific to 1995-2003 hardware
and reads as costume unless committed to fully. **Implies** SVG chrome gradients, a
CRT shader, chromatic aberration, dithering. **Fails** as kitsch that dates the
subject. **Right when** the audience shares the reference.

**Solarpunk.** Organic growth forms and botanical geometry under warm optimistic
light: curves derived from phyllotaxis, never arbitrary blobs, terracotta and sage
and brass, layouts that branch instead of stacking. **Implies** generative SVG
growth, warm gradients, curved layout paths, organic easing. **Fails** as generic
eco-branding with a leaf icon and a green button. **Right when** the work is climate,
agriculture, health, or civic.

## Motion-native

In these four the behavior **is** the aesthetic. A still screenshot cannot represent
them, which makes the `§12` reduced-motion design a first-class deliverable.

**Kinetic.** Nothing is at rest: type in perpetual motion, marquees running at
different rates by depth, letters responding to pointer velocity, composition
recomposing continuously. Stillness is used once, as punctuation. **Implies**
scroll-velocity input, variable-font axis animation, transform-only compositing.
**Fails** as exhausting, and unreadable when the thing in motion is the thing being
read. **Right when** the work is performance or sound.

**Physics-world.** Spring, inertia, mass, and collision are the interaction model.
Elements have weight, throwing them works, they settle rather than snap, and they
occupy space other elements respect. Nothing uses a duration; everything uses a
stiffness. **Implies** a physics loop, spring tokens instead of easing curves, a
valid resting layout. **Fails** as a toy when the physics never resolves into
something readable. **Right when** the play makes a point.

**Scroll-cinema.** The page is a film reel scrubbed by the scrollbar: scroll position
maps to a timeline, sections pin while their contents advance, and the sequence has
shots, cuts, and cadence. **Implies** pinned containers, scrubbed timelines,
`will-change` discipline, a real `§13` budget. **Fails** as hijacked scroll that
fights the user and strands anyone landing mid-page. **Right when** the work has
narrative order and one story to tell.

**Spatial / 3D-world.** The site is a navigable space with camera, depth, and
position. Sections are places, navigation is movement, and the sense of where you are
does the work a menu usually does. **Implies** WebGL or CSS 3D, a camera rig,
level-of-detail, a no-WebGL fallback per `§12`. **Fails** as a maze where nobody
finds the case study, which is `§7` violated structurally. **Right when** a flat page
would misrepresent the work.

## Technical and data

**Terminal.** Monospace throughout on a real fixed cell grid, blinking block cursor,
phosphor color on near-black, scanlines and slight CRT curvature at the edges, output
persisting in scrollback. **Implies** `ch` units, a monospace with box-drawing
coverage, a CRT shader, typed-output timing. **Fails** as a gimmick with a fake
prompt that takes three commands and breaks on the fourth. **Right when** the
terminal is where the subject's work happens.

**Blueprint.** Drawing conventions applied literally: dimension lines with arrowheads
and measurements, section callouts, leader lines to annotations, hatching, a title
block, a consistent line-weight hierarchy. **Implies** SVG line work, precise stroke
tokens, annotation positioning, a drafting typeface. **Fails** as decoration when the
dimensions are fake and measure nothing. **Right when** the callouts annotate real
work.

**Data-brutalist.** Dense tables, sparklines, and charts as the aesthetic itself,
never as supporting evidence. Rules are hairlines, numbers tabular, alignment
decimal, and the interest comes from the density of true information. **Implies**
`font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, table semantics, inline SVG charts. **Fails**
the moment the numbers are decorative, which breaks `§5` outright. **Right when**
`EVIDENCE.md` can carry every number on the page.

**Wireframe / vector.** Line art only: no fills, hidden-line removal, contours
describing volume through stroke alone, weight variation carrying depth. **Implies**
SVG or WebGL line rendering, hidden-line computation, stroke-only tokens, draw-on
animation. **Fails** as thin and cold at sizes where strokes vanish. **Right when**
the work is structural and the outline is the honest view.

## Textural

**Risograph.** Two or three spot inks printed in separate passes with visible
misregistration, halftone dots in the shadows, paper grain showing through, and
overprint areas producing a third color neither ink has. **Implies** separated
channels, `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, per-channel offset, a halftone shader, paper
per `§10`. **Fails** as a filter when the misregistration is uniform, since real
registration error drifts. **Right when** the subject prints.

**Xerox / degraded.** Photocopy artifacts as the medium: blown highlights, crushed
blacks, toner scatter at the edges, a slight skew, and generational loss where a copy
of a copy has lost its midtones. **Implies** threshold and dither passes, noise
displacement, per-element skew, a high-contrast duotone. **Fails** as illegible on
body copy instead of on images and headers. **Right when** the work is zine or
archival.

**Collage.** Layered scraps at mixed scale with torn edges, tape and staples, cast
shadows from real height differences, elements rotated off axis. The composition is
assembled, never laid out. **Implies** irregular SVG masks, per-element shadow
and rotation, generated paper and tape, deliberate z-order. **Fails** as chaos with
no reading order, losing `§6` immediately. **Right when** the practice is genuinely
multidisciplinary.

**Ink / sumi.** Brush dynamics as the whole language: strokes with real pressure
variation, wet bleed into fiber, dry-brush breakup at speed, negative space treated
as the subject. One color, one gesture per composition. **Implies** SVG
variable-width paths, bleed via displacement, generated fiber, stroke-order
animation. **Fails** as a stock brush texture, which reads as clip art instantly.
**Right when** restraint is the position.

## Reductive

**Radical minimalism.** Type and space, nothing else: no borders, no cards, no
shadows, no illustration. Hierarchy comes only from size, weight, and distance, and
the whitespace is measured, never left over. **Implies** one family with real
weights, a precise spatial scale, optical alignment, single-property motion.
**Fails** as unmemorable when the copy is weak, since there is nothing else to look
at. **Right when** the writing is strong.

**Monochrome plus one accent.** A single hue's full tonal range carries structure,
and exactly one accent sampled from reality per `§8` appears only where attention
must go. The accent never decorates. **Implies** an OKLCH lightness ramp, one accent
token, usage rules stated in `DIRECTION.md`. **Fails** as forgettable, the most
common way a run looks competent and generic at once. **Right when** it is the
discipline layer under a louder partner.

**ASCII / text-only.** The page is characters: art drawn in a fixed cell grid, layout
built from box-drawing glyphs, images dithered into character density. Nothing is
rendered that could not be pasted into a text file. **Implies** monospace with full
box-drawing coverage, `ch` and `lh` units, semantic HTML underneath per `§12`.
**Fails** as unreadable to screen readers and unusable below 400px. **Right when**
the constraint is the point.

---

## Collision

This is the most important section in the file. A single named style is one search
away from being everyone else's site. The un-templated work lives where two styles
are held in tension, because the constraints of one force the other to behave in ways
its own tradition never asks of it.

| Collision | What it produces that neither parent has |
|---|---|
| **Liquid glass over a blueprint substrate** | A technical drawing is flat and authoritative by convention. Put a refractive lens over it and the dimension lines bend as you scroll, so precision becomes something you look *through*. The drawing gains depth without losing its claim to accuracy. |
| **Risograph texture on a Swiss grid** | The grid asserts machine order; the misregistration asserts a hand and a press. Together they read as a printed object instead of a rendered page, and the grid stops looking like every other agency site because it is visibly ink. |
| **Terminal chrome around a physics world** | The monospace frame promises determinism and fixed cells. The contents obey springs and collide. A frame that cannot bend around contents that will not sit still is the whole idea, and neither style contains it alone. |
| **Editorial print with a spatial 3D reveal** | Columns, drop caps, marginalia, then the page turns out to have depth and the columns are planes standing in space. Reading becomes navigation and the reader's position in the document becomes literal. |
| **Brutalist structure with a cinematic grade** | Raw exposed structure and system fonts, lit with a single key and a vignette. The honesty stops reading as unfinished and starts reading as staged, a claim neither raw HTML nor a film grade makes on its own. |
| **Neumorphism inside radical minimalism** | The style that normally fails by covering a page in soft mush is reduced to one extruded object in an empty field. It becomes sculptural, and the contrast failure disappears because nothing has to be read off it. |
| **Ink gesture across data-brutalism** | Dense tabular numbers with one brush stroke laid over them. The gesture asserts that a person read these numbers and had a view, which a table cannot say and a painting cannot evidence. |
| **Vaporwave chrome under Swiss typography** | Y2K materials disciplined by an unforgiving grid and one type family. The nostalgia survives, the kitsch collapse does not, because the layout refuses to join in. |

**Picking a collision that serves the brief.** One parent comes from the archetype and
positioning in `BRAND.md`. The other comes from something materially true about the
subject: their medium, their tools, the physical object their work becomes, the room
they work in. Both must be defensible in one sentence each against `BRIEF.md`. If
only one is defensible, you have a style plus a decoration, and the decoration reads
as arbitrary to everyone who sees it.

**The load-bearing rule:** one parent carries structure, the other carries surface.
Two structural parents fight over the grid and produce mush. Two surface parents
produce noise with no bones. Name which parent is which in `DIRECTION.md` before you
build anything.

## Subversion

The second route out of template. Take one style and break exactly one of its own
rules, and the rule you break has to be the one the style is most identified by.
Break two and you have a different style executed badly.

- **Swiss where one element never obeys the grid.** A single photographic plate hangs
  past the margin in every section, at the same overhang each time. The grid is
  provable everywhere else, which is what makes the overhang read as a decision.
- **Brutalism with immaculate type.** Everything raw, default, unstyled, except the
  typography, which gets real optical sizing, hyphenation, and hung punctuation. The
  refusal to decorate becomes selective and therefore intentional.
- **Cinematic dark that turns the lights on once.** One section drops the grade
  entirely and goes flat daylight white. The return to darkness afterwards hits
  harder than the darkness ever did alone.
- **Glassmorphism with no blur.** The panels refract and catch light at their edges
  and nothing behind them softens. Legibility improves, `§12` gets easier, and the
  material reads as harder and more precise than glass usually does.
- **Editorial print where the margin is the main column.** Marginalia carries the
  primary narrative and the body text becomes the aside. The reader learns a new
  hierarchy in about four seconds and remembers it.
- **Terminal with one full-color photograph.** Everything is phosphor and monospace
  except a single image at full fidelity. It becomes the most important object on the
  site with no layout emphasis at all.

State the broken rule explicitly in `DIRECTION.md`. A subversion nobody can name is
indistinguishable from an inconsistency.

## The guardrails

This section is `§3` enforced.

- **The vocabulary names a starting position, never a destination.** Ship a named
  style unmodified and the run failed. No entry above is a finished answer.
- **Every run states in `DIRECTION.md` what it did to the style that nobody else
  does** — the collision, subversion, or invention applied, in one sentence a
  stranger could check the site against.
- **The vision beats the style.** If the vision or `BRIEF.md` says "quiet, like a
  printed book," liquid glass is off the table regardless of how good the prototype
  looks. A prototype is not an argument against the intake from `§0`.
- **The archetype from `BRAND.md` pulls a shortlist, never a single answer.** It
  narrows the field to three or four candidates. Treating it as a lookup table is how
  every Sage becomes Swiss and every Creator becomes neo-brutalist.
- **Anti-positioning from `BRAND.md` bans styles outright.** If the strategy says
  "never look like a crypto site," glow-neon and chrome are gone. Honor it as
  absolutely as the `§0` do-nots.
- **The list is open.** Invent one, name it, describe it in the format above, and add
  it to the run. An invented style with a real name and stated mechanics beats the
  best-executed entry on this page, because nobody can pattern-match it.

## Style and accessibility

`§12` is **[HARD]**. These styles fight it hardest, and each ships with its fix or
does not ship.

| Style | What it fights | The fix that ships |
|---|---|---|
| **Neumorphism** | Form is shadow on one hue, so nothing has a contrast ratio | Extrusion is for containers only. Every label, value, and control state gets a real foreground token at ≥4.5:1. Focus is a hard visible ring, never a deeper shadow. |
| **Glassmorphism / liquid glass** | Text contrast changes with whatever scrolls behind it | An opaque or near-opaque scrim behind every text run, measured against the *worst* frame of the moving substrate, never a screenshot. |
| **Cinematic dark** | Vignette, grade, and grain push small type below threshold | Measure contrast on the rendered pixels after grade and grain, not on the tokens. Body copy stays out of the vignette falloff. Grain opacity drops on text layers. |
| **Kinetic / physics / scroll-cinema** | Motion is the design, so removing motion removes the site | An art-directed still per `§12`: a composed frame with type at rest that someone designed. Scroll-cinema degrades to a paginated document, same content, same order. |
| **Spatial / 3D-world** | Navigation depends on a camera and a GPU | Keyboard traversal between named places, a text route to every section, and a no-WebGL fallback that is a real page, never an apology. |
| **Terminal** | Scanlines and CRT curvature reduce legibility and can trigger | Curvature and scanline opacity behind `prefers-reduced-motion` plus a visible toggle. Body text renders on the flat layer above the effect. |
| **ASCII / text-only** | Screen readers read the art as character soup | `aria-hidden` on the art, `role="img"` with a written alt on the block, and real semantic HTML carrying the content underneath. |
| **Glow-neon / vaporwave** | Saturated emission on dark causes halation and fringing | Glow applies to non-text elements only. Text uses a desaturated stop of the same hue at full contrast. Chromatic aberration never touches a glyph. |
| **Data-brutalist** | Density defeats zoom and reflow | Real table semantics with scoped headers, horizontal scroll containers that are keyboard reachable, and a stated minimum readable width. |

## Light and dark as two designs

Per [`CRAFT.md`](./CRAFT.md)'s art-directed modes, a style often needs a genuinely
different treatment in each mode. Never `filter: invert()`. Choose per-mode ink,
substrate, shadow direction, and accent chroma deliberately. These break under naive
inversion:

- **Neumorphism.** Inverting the shadow pair puts the light source underneath, which
  no physical object does. Keep the light direction identical in both modes and
  change only the surface hue and the shadow spread.
- **Glassmorphism.** Blur reads as depth on dark and as haze on light. Light mode
  needs more opacity, a heavier border, and less blur to say the same thing.
- **Cinematic dark.** There is no light version of a lit set. Light mode is a second
  art direction: a printed still with the grade baked in as a duotone, no vignette,
  no bloom.
- **Glow / neon.** Emission requires darkness. In light mode the glow becomes ink
  saturation and weight, and the accent moves from emissive to dense.
- **Risograph.** Paper is the substrate. Dark mode is a black-paper print run with
  inks chosen for it, and the halftone dot inverts to open rather than filled.
- **Blueprint.** White-on-blue and blue-on-white are both real print conventions.
  Switch between them on purpose, with line weights retuned, since hairlines that
  read on dark disappear on white.
- **Aurora / mesh.** OKLCH stops that stay saturated on dark go chalky on light. Each
  mode needs its own stop list, never a lightness shift.

Declare in `DIRECTION.md` whether the two modes are one design in two palettes or two
art directions. If the chosen style appears above, the answer is two art directions,
and both get built and screenshotted under `§14`.

# Direction — Said Mohaddes Sadeqi · sadeqi.me

**Status: Loop 2a, pre-Gate-B1.** Three concepts below. One gets chosen, the rest of
this file is completed in 2b.

Reads from `BRIEF.md` § 9 translation table. Archetype **Outlaw / Caregiver**,
"an argument delivered as an embrace."

---

## Fixed across all three concepts

These come from the translation table and do not vary by concept.

### Palette — sampled, literal AAA, both modes

Sampled from a photograph of the **Hari Rud at Herat** (Wikimedia Commons,
`Herat_Hari_Rud_bridge.jpg`), the river of the city where the subject's story starts.
He asked for "the green colors of the rivers." Dominant cluster `#9FB4AD`, mean
`#6C8474`. Pale mineral river-green, not eco-green, because that is what that river is.

| Token | Dark (default) | Ratio | Light | Ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--substrate` | `#0B0F0D` | — | `#F4F2EC` | — |
| `--raised` | `#141A17` | — | `#E8E5DC` | — |
| `--ink` (body) | `#F4F2EC` | 17.24:1 | `#0B0F0D` | 17.24:1 |
| `--ink-dim` | `#C9CFCB` | 12.19:1 | `#2B443B` | 9.41:1 |
| `--river` (accent) | `#9FB4AD` | **8.83:1** | `#375349` | **7.52:1** |
| `--river-lift` (hover/focus) | `#B6C9C2` | 11.14:1 | `#2B443B` | 9.41:1 |
| `--amber` (rare, second accent) | `#C99A56` | 7.57:1 | — | — |

Every value clears **7:1 — literal WCAG AAA**, his explicit choice. Verified by
computation, not by eye. Two art directions, not one inverted palette: dark is lit,
light is printed.

`--amber` is sampled from the golden-hour foliage in his own supplied photograph. It
appears at most twice per page and never on a link.

### Type

Two families.

- **Atkinson Hyperlegible** — body *and* display. Designed by the Braille Institute
  for low-vision readers: disambiguated letterforms, exaggerated apertures, distinct
  I/l/1 and O/0. Chosen because it is materially true rather than decorative — the
  face on this site exists for the person the site is addressed to. Setting it at
  display scale is the subversion; nobody uses it as a display face.
- **IBM Plex Mono** — structural labels only: landmark names, status tags, focus-order
  numbers, figures. Never body copy.

Both self-hosted, subset, `font-display: swap` (`§9`). Site is English-only; if Dari
or Persian is added later, Atkinson does not cover Arabic script and a second face is
required (`§17`).

### Banned outright (from anti-positioning)

Logo wall. Badge row. Metric hero. Autoplay anything. Gradient mesh. Card grid by
reflex. Inspiration framing. Overlay-widget aesthetics. Any version number or "beta
built" claim on Third Eye World.

### The audio rule, common to all three

The voice greeting he asked for — *"welcome, you are not alone"* — is **offered, never
fired.** No autoplay: browsers block it, and a page that talks over a screen reader is
the exact failure this site argues against. It sits first in DOM order after the `h1`,
as a real `<button>`, so a screen-reader user meets it immediately by traversal and a
sighted user meets it as the first thing on the page. Recorded in his own voice, not
synthesized. Transcript visible, not hidden.

---

## Concept 1 — OUTLINE  *(recommended)*

### The collision

> **The accessibility tree is the visible design** — the structure a screen reader
> traverses is promoted to the artwork, and the sighted rendering is a treatment of
> it rather than the other way round.

**Structural parent:** an invented style, *Screen-reader-first / Outline* (below).
**Surface parent:** Editorial print — generous measure, real hyphenation, warm
substrate, marginalia. This is the Caregiver half, and it is what stops the structure
reading as a devtools screenshot.

### The invented style — *Outline*

Named and specified per `STYLES.md` § guardrails ("the list is open").

> Landmarks, heading levels, and focus order are the composition. Section boundaries
> are drawn because they are real `<section>` elements with real labels. Heading rank
> is expressed as an actual typographic scale, so `h2` and `h3` differ by more than
> convention. The focus ring is a primary design element with its own art direction,
> not a browser default someone forgot to remove. The skip link is not hidden — it is
> among the largest elements on the first screen.
> **Implies** semantic HTML rendered honestly, `:focus-visible` as a designed state,
> a visible landmark map, monospace structure labels.
> **Fails** as a devtools inspector panel when the typography is not beautiful enough
> to carry it, or as a lecture when the labels explain themselves at the visitor.
> **Right when** the subject's entire argument is that the non-visual layer deserves
> to be the designed one — which is exactly `BRIEF.md` §4.

### Opening move (first three seconds)

Full-viewport, one sentence at display scale, set in the face built for low vision:

> **it is ok if eyes are not at 100%**

Beneath it, one control — *Listen* — and nothing else above the fold. No photo, no
nav bar, no scroll cue. The page states its claim and offers the voice. A screen
reader arriving here reads the `h1`, then immediately meets the button. A sighted
visitor sees the same two objects. **Both audiences receive the same first screen in
the same order.** That is the entire thesis, executed structurally rather than
described.

### How projects are presented

Not cards. **A vertical index of numbered stops**, one per project, each carrying a
plainly-stated status tag in mono: `SHIPPED 2022` · `REBUILDING` · `FOUNDER, NOT
BUILDER` · `SPECIFICATION`. The proof rank is visible on the page. This is the
anti-inflation position made into a visual system — the honest label is the design,
and a recruiter reads the whole slate in one pass.

### Navigation

The heading outline itself, persistent in the left margin on desktop and as a real
`<nav>` disclosure on mobile. It is simultaneously the table of contents, the landmark
map, and the current-position indicator. Invented for this subject rather than a top
bar: for a screen-reader user the outline *is* how the site is navigated, so making it
visible hands the sighted visitor the same instrument.

### Section list and order

1. Hero — the claim and the Listen control
2. What he stands for — three sentences, his own
3. The proof — Third Eye Kit, 2022, real hardware photographs
4. The active work — Third Eye World, and what broke
5. The slate — all five projects with honest status
6. Who he is — the photograph, the origin, plainly
7. The ask — contact
8. Footer — accessibility statement, attribution (`§19`)

---

## Concept 2 — FIELD REPORT

### The collision

> **A 2022 engineering proposal, grown up** — blueprint drafting convention carrying
> the structure, risograph ink carrying the surface, so the site reads as a printed
> technical document rather than a rendered page.

**Structural parent:** Blueprint — dimension lines that measure real objects, section
callouts, leader lines into annotations, a title block per sheet.
**Surface parent:** Risograph — two spot inks (river green, amber), visible
misregistration that drifts rather than repeats, halftone in the shadows, paper tooth.

Defensible because he *has* the drawings: four real SVG schematics (system
architecture, electronics wiring, exo state machine, haptic body map) plus a proposal
PDF with genuine hardware photographs. The callouts annotate real work, which is the
exact condition `STYLES.md` sets for blueprint not being decoration.

### Opening move

An engineering title block, full width, filled with true values: subject, project,
sheet 1 of 7, revision, date, and the status field reading `IN REBUILD`. The Listen
control sits in the title block as a field like any other.

### How projects are presented

**As drawing sheets.** Each project is a sheet with its own title block and status
field; the specification-only projects are sheets stamped `SPECIFICATION — NOT BUILT`,
which turns the weakest evidence into the most honest-looking object on the site.

### Navigation

A sheet index — the drawing-set convention, numbered, always visible.

### Risk, stated

It is about the hardware, and the hardware is his strongest evidence. But the thesis —
sight is not required — becomes something the site *says* rather than something it
*does*. It also concedes the competitive gap: it is a beautiful visual-first document,
which is what all nine peers already ship.

---

## Concept 3 — THE ROUTE

### The collision

> **The site guides you the way his device guides someone** — wayfinding structure
> carrying the bones, radical minimalism carrying the surface, so arriving somewhere
> is the interaction model and there is nothing on screen that is not a landmark.

**Structural parent:** Spatial wayfinding, flattened — sections are *places* with
names, distances, and arrival states. Navigation is movement between them, announced.
**Surface parent:** Radical minimalism — type and space only, no borders, no cards,
one accent.

Defensible because his hardware's literal job is navigation: ultrasonic distance,
GPS, haptic guidance, "navigation was hard and required multiple gestures."

### Opening move

A single named place — `START` — and a distance to the next one. The Listen control
announces where you are. Movement between places is a real route with a stated
position, so a keyboard user and a screen-reader user get the *better* experience,
not the equivalent one.

### How projects are presented

**As arrivals along a route**, in chronological order, with the distance between them
stated in years. 2022 to now is short, and saying so is more honest than padding it.

### Navigation

The route itself. Previous place, current place, next place — always announced, always
keyboard-driven.

### Risk, stated

`§7`. Wayfinding is memorable, and it can become more memorable than the case study it
frames. It also risks the maze failure `STYLES.md` names for spatial work: a recruiter
with four minutes must never have to *travel* to the evidence.

---

## Rejected, and why (`§4`)

**"Waveform."** The site's entire visual language derived from audio and haptic
signal traces — pulse patterns as rules, dividers, and heading underlines. Rejected on
two counts. It is the category reflex: anything sound-adjacent reaches for a
visualizer, and it would be guessable from "portfolio for someone who builds audio
accessibility tools" alone. And the traces would be decorative rather than real — no
signal logs exist in evidence — which is the precise failure `STYLES.md` names for
data-brutalism and which `§5` bans in spirit.

---

## To be completed in 2b (post-B1)

Technique assignment per section · motion spec · both performance budget tiers ·
prototype results including failures · what was invented, final.

+bar: for a screen-reader user the outline *is* how the site is navigated, so making it
+visible hands the sighted visitor the same instrument.
+### Section list and order
+1. Hero — the claim and the Listen control
+2. What he stands for — three sentences, his own
+3. The proof — Third Eye Kit, 2022, real hardware photographs
+4. The active work — Third Eye World, and what broke
+5. The slate — all five projects with honest status
+6. Who he is — the photograph, the origin, plainly
+7. The ask — contact
+8. Footer — accessibility statement, attribution (`§19`)
+## Concept 2 — FIELD REPORT
+### The collision
+> **A 2022 engineering proposal, grown up** — blueprint drafting convention carrying
+> the structure, risograph ink carrying the surface, so the site reads as a printed
+> technical document rather than a rendered page.
+**Structural parent:** Blueprint — dimension lines that measure real objects, section
+callouts, leader lines into annotations, a title block per sheet.
+**Surface parent:** Risograph — two spot inks (river green, amber), visible
+misregistration that drifts rather than repeats, halftone in the shadows, paper tooth.
+Defensible because he *has* the drawings: four real SVG schematics (system
+architecture, electronics wiring, exo state machine, haptic body map) plus a proposal
+PDF with genuine hardware photographs. The callouts annotate real work, which is the
+exact condition `STYLES.md` sets for blueprint not being decoration.
+### Opening move
+An engineering title block, full width, filled with true values: subject, project,
+sheet 1 of 7, revision, date, and the status field reading `IN REBUILD`. The Listen
+control sits in the title block as a field like any other.
+### How projects are presented
+**As drawing sheets.** Each project is a sheet with its own title block and status
+field; the specification-only projects are sheets stamped `SPECIFICATION — NOT BUILT`,
+which turns the weakest evidence into the most honest-looking object on the site.
+### Navigation
+A sheet index — the drawing-set convention, numbered, always visible.
+### Risk, stated
+It is about the hardware, and the hardware is his strongest evidence. But the thesis —
+sight is not required — becomes something the site *says* rather than something it
+*does*. It also concedes the competitive gap: it is a beautiful visual-first document,
+which is what all nine peers already ship.
+## Concept 3 — THE ROUTE
+### The collision
+> **The site guides you the way his device guides someone** — wayfinding structure
+> carrying the bones, radical minimalism carrying the surface, so arriving somewhere
+> is the interaction model and there is nothing on screen that is not a landmark.
+**Structural parent:** Spatial wayfinding, flattened — sections are *places* with
+names, distances, and arrival states. Navigation is movement between them, announced.
+**Surface parent:** Radical minimalism — type and space only, no borders, no cards,
+one accent.
+Defensible because his hardware's literal job is navigation: ultrasonic distance,
+GPS, haptic guidance, "navigation was hard and required multiple gestures."
+### Opening move
+A single named place — `START` — and a distance to the next one. The Listen control
+announces where you are. Movement between places is a real route with a stated
+position, so a keyboard user and a screen-reader user get the *better* experience,
+not the equivalent one.
+### How projects are presented
+**As arrivals along a route**, in chronological order, with the distance between them
+stated in years. 2022 to now is short, and saying so is more honest than padding it.
+### Navigation
+The route itself. Previous place, current place, next place — always announced, always
+keyboard-driven.
+### Risk, stated
+`§7`. Wayfinding is memorable, and it can become more memorable than the case study it
+frames. It also risks the maze failure `STYLES.md` names for spatial work: a recruiter
+with four minutes must never have to *travel* to the evidence.

+signal traces — pulse patterns as rules, dividers, and heading underlines. Rejected on

+visualizer, and it would be guessable from "portfolio for someone who builds audio
+accessibility tools" alone. And the traces would be decorative rather than real — no
+signal logs exist in evidence — which is the precise failure `STYLES.md` names for
+data-brutalism and which `§5` bans in spirit.
+## To be completed in 2b (post-B1)
+Technique assignment per section · motion spec · both performance budget tiers ·
+prototype results including failures · what was invented, final.

content.text:
Six renders in flight. While they come back, here's what you're choosing between — react now if any of it is wrong, it's far cheaper than iterating on images.

**Fixed across all three,** because it comes from the strategy rather than the concept:

*Type.* Body and display are both **Atkinson Hyperlegible** — the face the Braille Institute designed for low-vision readers, with disambiguated letterforms and exaggerated apertures. It's on the site because it's materially true, not because it's a nice typeface. Setting it at display scale is the subversion; nobody uses it that way. **IBM Plex Mono** carries structural labels only.

*The voice.* Offered, never fired. First in DOM order after the headline, as a real button, recorded in your own voice rather than synthesized, transcript visible. A screen-reader user meets it immediately by traversal; a sighted user meets it as the first object on the page. Same greeting, same position, both audiences.

---

**1 · OUTLINE** *(recommended)*

The accessibility tree becomes the visible design. The structure a screen reader walks — landmarks, heading levels, focus order — is promoted to the artwork, and the sighted rendering is a treatment of it rather than the other way round. The skip link isn't hidden; it's one of the largest things on the first screen.

You open on one sentence at full scale — *it is ok if eyes are not at 100%* — and a single Listen control. No photo, no nav bar, no scroll cue. Projects are a numbered index with the status stated in mono: `REBUILDING`, `SHIPPED 2022`, `FOUNDER, NOT BUILDER`, `SPECIFICATION`. Navigation is the heading outline itself, always visible.

This is an invented style, not one off the shelf. It occupies the gap the peer chart found, and it makes your thesis structural instead of stated. Its failure mode is looking like a devtools panel, which is why editorial warmth carries the surface.

**2 · FIELD REPORT**

Your 2022 engineering proposal, grown up. Blueprint drafting carries the bones — dimension lines that measure real objects, callouts, a title block per sheet. Risograph ink carries the surface: two spot inks, drifting misregistration, halftone, paper tooth on black paper.

Defensible because you actually have the drawings. Each project is a drawing sheet, and the spec-only ones get stamped `SPECIFICATION — NOT BUILT`, which turns your weakest evidence into the most honest-looking object on the site.

The cost: it's about the hardware. Your thesis becomes something the site *says* rather than something it *does* — and it concedes the gap, because a beautiful visual-first document is what all nine peers already ship.

**3 · THE ROUTE**

The site guides you the way your device guides someone. Sections are named places with distances and arrival states; navigation is movement, announced. Radical minimalism on the surface — type and space, no borders, no cards. Projects are arrivals in chronological order with the gap between them stated in years, and the vertical spacing is proportional to elapsed time, so the space carries the data.

The risk is §7: wayfinding is memorable and could end up more memorable than the case study. A recruiter with four minutes must never have to *travel* to the evidence.

---

**Rejected, so you can see the range:** "Waveform" — the whole visual language built from audio and haptic signal traces. It's the category reflex, guessable from your job description alone, and the traces would be decorative rather than real data, which breaks §5 in spirit.

Images land shortly. You can pick one concept, or take pieces across them.
